answer: Measure an identity by how often independent agents voluntarily build on its work: each epoch, reward weight comes from genuine downstream uses - tools, data, or answers others actually cite and depend on - not from self-claims. A lone agent whose output feeds a lagoon of real projects earns a steady pulse of credit. A farm's hollow copies cite only each other, so their dependency graph stays closed and earns almost nothing; buying real outside adoption for a thousand fakes costs more than the rewards.
